rubrics.rubric: Does the response provide exactly three distinct WIC clinic options in ranked order?
criterion: The answer lists exactly three clinic options.
The three clinics are explicitly ranked or ordered from first to third.
Each clinic named is an actual clinic from the Washington WIC clinic list.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response identify Yakima NHS-Yakima as the best clinic for this family?
criterion: The top-ranked clinic is Yakima NHS-Yakima.
The clinic details include phone number 509-454-4143.
The clinic details include address 12 South 8th St, Yakima, WA, 98907.
The ranking rationale cites weekday hours until 6:30 p.m. and Saturday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. as the strongest schedule fit.

rubrics.rubric: Does the shortlist keep the other recommendations centered on practical Yakima-area alternatives?
criterion: The second- and third-ranked options are in Yakima or are explicitly justified despite being farther from ZIP code 98902.
The shortlist does not treat Grandview, Granger, Toppenish, or Wapato as default top-three choices without a stated access advantage.
The rationale weighs both travel practicality and scheduling access.

rubrics.rubric: Does the shortlist include Yakima Valley FWC-West Valley as a strong late-day weekday alternative?
criterion: The shortlist includes Yakima Valley FWC-West Valley.
Its weekday hours are described as 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.
The answer notes that it has no Saturday hours.
The rationale treats it as a strong late-day weekday option rather than the best Saturday fit.

rubrics.rubric: Does the shortlist include a Yakima-area Saturday alternative besides the top clinic and describe its limited Saturday access correctly?
criterion: The shortlist includes Yakima Valley FWC-Yakima Memorial Hospital or Yakima Valley FWC-Yakima.
If Yakima Valley FWC-Yakima Memorial Hospital is included, the answer states that it is open on the 2nd Saturday of the month from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
If Yakima Valley FWC-Yakima is included, the answer states that it is open on the 3rd Saturday of the month from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.
The rationale treats monthly Saturday availability as limited access rather than weekly Saturday access.

rubrics.rubric: Does each clinic entry include the routing information needed for the office to act on the recommendation?
criterion: Each clinic entry includes the clinic name.
Each clinic entry includes the phone number.
Each clinic entry includes the full street address.
Each clinic entry includes scheduling details or special notes that affect suitability.

rubrics.rubric: Does the ranking rationale explicitly use the caregiver's scheduling constraint of being unavailable before 4:30 p.m. on weekdays?
criterion: At least one clinic is favored because it stays open after 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.
Clinics that close at 5:00 p.m. are treated as weaker weekday fits than clinics that stay open until 6:00 p.m. or 6:30 p.m.
Saturday availability is discussed as an alternative when weekday timing is difficult.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response avoid recommending restricted or clearly less suitable clinics without necessary caveats?
criterion: The answer does not recommend Yakama Nation-Toppenish without stating that it serves only individuals enrolled in or descended from a federally recognized tribe.
The answer does not recommend Yakama Nation-White Swan without stating the same tribal eligibility restriction and its highly limited schedule.
The answer does not present a limited-access clinic as broadly available if the spreadsheet shows monthly-only or otherwise narrow availability.

rubrics.rubric: Does the shortlist describe clinic hours and special notes accurately?
criterion: The answer distinguishes weekly Saturday hours from 2nd-Saturday-only or 3rd-Saturday-only access.
The answer distinguishes weekday closing times of 6:30 p.m., 6:00 p.m., and 5:00 p.m. instead of flattening them together.
Any lunch closure or special-note detail included in the answer matches the spreadsheet.

rubrics.rubric: Does the pre-send checklist capture the formula section requirements without guessing unsupported values?
criterion: The checklist notes that the formula section applies only if supplemental formula is being requested.
The checklist includes formula type from section 2A and ounces per day from section 2B as missing items that require provider confirmation.
The checklist includes ready-to-feed medical-need explanation and pharmacy submission status from sections 2C and 2D if applicable.
The checklist explicitly avoids inventing formula details that still require provider confirmation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the pre-send checklist capture the child-specific supplemental food section relevant to a 19-month-old?
criterion: The checklist treats the patient as a child age 12 to 23 months within section 3A.
The checklist notes that section 3A may require a milk or yogurt selection if the provider indicates one.
The checklist notes that food restrictions should be entered only if the provider specifies them.
